title: Biased Fourier coefficients under permutation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $p\in(0,1)$, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The biased Fourier coefficient of the function obtained by permuting the input of $f$ by $\sigma$, at $S$, equals the biased Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the image of $S$ under the inverse permutation.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ is a permutation of the coordinates
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
